name: Renew the lease
description:
THE LEASE IS THE DATABASE'S CLOCK and always was: now() + $2 seconds is computed here, the runner never sends a timestamp, and moving the caller onto a machine whose clock nobody controls costs nothing because of it. No indexed column changes, so the update stays heap-only -- the reason matches carries fillfactor 70 and the reason lease_expires_at is deliberately not indexed.

ANSWERS 200 EVEN WHEN NOTHING MOVED, and that is not sloppiness. Over a WAN a runner must tell two failures apart: applied:false means the statement ran and matched no row, so the claim is genuinely gone and the match should halt; a transport error means almost nothing and should be retried, because the renew interval is roughly a tenth of the lease. A 409 here would collapse the two into one, and the second is the common one.

input.query: UPDATE matches SET lease_expires_at = now() + ($2)::int * interval '1 second' WHERE id = ($4)::uuid AND claim_token = ($1)::uuid AND status = 'running' AND played_by = ($3)::uuid AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM live_runners lr WHERE lr.id = ($3)::uuid)

tasks.name: Read the new lease back
tasks.description: The runner could not see its own runway before and now needs to: a renew can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with its claim, and the decision to halt is 'has lease_expires_at passed', which is a value only the server holds.

input.query: SELECT m.lease_expires_at AS lease_expires_at FROM matches m WHERE m.id = ($1)::uuid AND m.claim_token = ($2)::uuid
